newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan to allow SIMEX, CME stock futures from Aug 1.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan to allow SIMEX, CME stock futures from Aug 1.

text.p: Taiwan's Securities and Futures Commission said on Monday it would lift a ban on local trading of offshore Taiwan stock-index futures offered in Singapore and Chicago from August 1.

A senior SFC official said a formal announcement would be made on Tuesday clearing the way for local trading of Taiwan index-linked contracts launched over Taipei's objections on January 9 by the Singapore International Monetary Exchange and the Chicago Mercantile Exchange.
"We will announce it tomorrow the approval of the SIMEX and CME's Taiwan-stock index contracts," the official told Reuters by telephone. "Local investors can start trading on August 1."
The official declined to give further details.
Taiwan had said in April that it would allow trading of the offshore stock-index futures on June 1, but postponed the liberalisation without official explanation.
Sources said the SIMEX and CME contracts were included in a package of approvals for local trading of overseas derivatives.
Taiwan stock-index options launched on January 9 by San Francisco's Pacific Stock Exchange, which have not generated much trading interest, are not on the list, the sources said.

Trading volume for the SIMEX and CME contracts remains relatively small, and analysts said the entry of risk-loving investors from Taiwan could provide the much-needed liquidity that could ignite competitive trade.

"Taiwan investors can provide a significant turnover volumes for the Singapore and Chicago contracts," a Taipei futures broker said. "Local investors will love to trade the stock-index futures that are based on Taiwan's stocks."
An August 1 launch would give the offshore exchanges a brief head start on stock-index derivatives expected to be launched in Taiwan's own futures exchange, scheduled to open in October.
The long-delayed establishment of Taiwan's first futures exchange had been planned for July but was slowed by legislative wrangling and regulatory red tape.
Regulators said the opening now was on track.
"The target date to open Taiwan's futures exchange is still in October," another SFC official said.
